source.title: Exponential Moving Average of Weights in Deep Learning: Dynamics and Benefits
source.authors: Daniel Morales-Brotons; Thijs Vogels; H. Hendrikx

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether weight averaging changes held-out image-classification performance, using EMA rather than the claim versions’ specified interventions or measurements.
record.gate_note: The study compares EMA and momentum-SGD test accuracy on natural image datasets. It does not test memorization of random labels, width beyond interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size gaps, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests EMA weight averaging, which none of V1–V8 names. It does not compare adaptive optimizers, batch sizes, dropout, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, or widths beyond interpolation, and does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or remove memorized examples. Its partially noisy-label experiments do not test V1's natural-label versus fully random-label comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase correctly captures the main accuracy-selected EMA results and their similarity to SWA. It needs qualification if read as covering every EMA configuration: loss-selected VGG-16 has lower accuracy than baseline, and Appendix A.1 reports that EMA with step decay only matches SGD. The authors additionally conclude that EMA improves label-noise robustness, prediction consistency, calibration, and transferability in their image-classification experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses EMA of momentum-SGD weights and compares it with the same SGD trajectory; it does not reproduce any listed version’s intervention or measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: EMA selection criterion (best validation accuracy or lowest validation loss), EMA decay, learning-rate schedule, and recomputation of batch-normalization statistics affect reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation-accuracy-selected EMA improves test accuracy over momentum SGD in all five Table 1 comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EMA with validation-selected early stopping can improve image-classification test accuracy over its underlying momentum-SGD baseline.

record.problems: The study focuses on image-classification benchmarks; its reported accuracy comparisons do not report training error or directly measure the train-test gap. Results are means of 3 runs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows bearing on the claim versions were identified. Other reported outcomes concern label-noise robustness, prediction consistency, calibration, transfer learning, and training dynamics, rather than the mapped versions’ specified measures.

untested.parts: Matched training recipes on natural and fully random labels, including random-label fitting and chance-level held-out accuracy.
Test-error changes when widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and changes to the training recipe.
Dropout interventions, training-set size, excessive dropout, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: EMA and SGD here both use momentum-SGD training; averaging weights is not an adaptive-optimizer comparison. Memorizing approximately 40% human-corrupted labels while retaining clean-label signal does not establish V1's fully random-label result. No omitted result tests a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold and test-error trajectory.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning breadth, weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to train-test gaps.
Removal and retraining on memorized examples.
